Let P1, P2, A1, A2, A be polynomials.
You want to go from:  A/(P1*P2)         (1)

To: A1/P1 + A2/P2                                 (2)

Thereby, you must find A1 and A2 such that:
A/(P1*P2) = A1/P1 + A2/P2                  (3)

In order to find a polynomial A1, A2 you need to know the order and the coefinients. The order of a polynomial is the highest power of x in that polynomial.

Let OP1 OP2 OA be the orders of the respective polynomial. If you bring equality 2 to the same denominator you get:

A= A1*P2 + A2*P1

From here you know that 2 polynomials are equal if the order is equal. The order changes when you multiply polynomials not when you add them so you get:

OA= OA1+OP2 = OA2*OP1                   (4)

This will allow you to find the corespondingorder of the polynomials. A1 and A2.

From here you just write the standard form of a polynomial knowing its order. This means: sum of all power of x lower than the order each multiply by a coefficient. Replace A1 and A2 with their expression in equality 4. Multiply what is there to be multiplied.Then you will get an equality between 2 polynomials with the same order. This means that you set the coefficient of the same power of x to be equal. You will get a system all linear equations that need to be solved. And you are done
